item.text:
**Diagnosis:** [`subscriptionExpires()`](/app/packages/components/containers/payments/subscription/helpers/payment.ts:120) always prefers `UpcomingSubscription`, so it can select the future term’s renewal state, plan name, and `PeriodEnd`. It has no cancellation context.

The cancellation screens also read dates directly. [`CancelSubscriptionModal.tsx`](/app/packages/components/containers/payments/subscription/cancelSubscription/CancelSubscriptionModal.tsx:34) and the [`b2cCommonConfig.tsx`](/app/packages/components/containers/payments/subscription/cancellationFlow/config/b2cCommonConfig.tsx:48) and [`b2bCommonConfig.tsx`](/app/packages/components/containers/payments/subscription/cancellationFlow/config/b2bCommonConfig.tsx:48) `ExpirationTime` components prefer the upcoming term. Those displays need to use the utility’s active-term expiration during cancellation.

The fix should add an optional cancellation context: when it is active or current auto-renew is disabled, return the current term’s `PeriodEnd` and available plan name with `subscriptionExpiresSoon: true`, `renewDisabled: true`, and `renewEnabled: false`. Preserve the existing upcoming-term behavior otherwise, and leave the free-plan result unchanged. Existing [`CancelSubscriptionModal.test.tsx`](/app/packages/components/containers/payments/subscription/cancelSubscription/CancelSubscriptionModal.test.tsx:53) explicitly expects the incorrect upcoming date; tests do not cover distinct current and upcoming plan names.

No project source or tests were edited in this diagnosis-only pass. Findings are recorded in [.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md](/app/.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md).
